result.title: From Natural Language Intent to Executable Control: Hierarchical Feedback-Guided LLM Planning for Multi-component Cyber-Physical Systems
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) provide a convenient interface for translating natural language commands into task plans for cyber-physical systems (CPSs). However, two gaps hinder their use for real execution: generated plans may misinterpret or omit the user's intent, and even a logically plausible plan may be infeasible under component dynamics, interactions, or safety constraints. Existing LLM-based planning approaches often lack informative feedback on why a generated plan fails, providing little guidance for revising the plan accordingly. To address these challenges, we present a hierarchical feedback framework that uses different types of feedback information to guide LLMs in generating executable plans for CPSs. We prompt LLMs to generate both a structured task plan and corresponding signal temporal logic (STL) constraints, and design a sound algorithm that identifies definite contradictions between them and provides feedback for revising inconsistencies. At the execution level, when control synthesis fails, we extract different types of diagnostic information, such as violated constraints and conflicting component assignments, and feed them back to guide task replanning. Experiments on seven heterogeneous multi-component CPS scenarios have shown that our framework can generate executable plans and feasible control executions that satisfy the original natural language missions with a success rate of 87.9% with GPT-5.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文面向多组件信息物理系统，提出分层反馈框架：让 LLM 同时生成结构化任务计划与 STL 约束，用可判定算法找出二者矛盾并在控制综合失败时回传诊断信息，引导重新规划，在 7 个场景中取得 87.9% 执行成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 主题为 CPS 控制合成与 STL 约束校验，不涉及视觉或多模态内部状态、latent 推理状态生成；其中的反馈机制只是通用规划修复环，未提供可核查的 LVR 方法或评价线索。
